claims: As of mid-March 2026, NASA is tracking several small near-Earth asteroids.
Asteroid 2026 EG1 is approximately 20-40 feet in size.
Asteroid 2026 EG1 safely passed within 198,000 miles on March 13, 2026.
Asteroid 2026 EG1 passed closer than the moon on March 13, 2026.
Routine close approaches are closely monitored by the NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL).
None of the small near-Earth asteroids tracked by NASA as of mid-March 2026 pose an immediate threat.
No dangerous impacts from the small near-Earth asteroids tracked by NASA as of mid-March 2026 are predicted for the next century.
Asteroids 2026 CS, 2026 BY1, and 2026 BU2 are smaller asteroids.
Asteroids 2026 CS, 2026 BY1, and 2026 BU2 approached within millions of miles in February 2026.
Asteroid Apophis is scheduled for a very close visible flyby on April 13, 2029.
Asteroid Apophis will pass within 19,000 miles on April 13, 2029.
Asteroid Bennu is categorized as potentially hazardous.
Asteroid Bennu has a 1 in 2,700 chance of collision by 2182.
